## Purpose

Recover a repair-no-progress incident when its latest delegate actually closed
PASS without introducing a commit and daemon-recorded CI is fully green on the
current canonical subject. The local operator or the live project supervisor can
review a read-only preview and apply its exact command.

## When a playbook uses it

Use after inspecting an escalated repair operation. Keep the default `dry_run`
until the supervisor has reviewed the exact subject, close audit, successor fence,
evidence and planned steps. Apply requires the returned snapshot and identities.

## How it works internally

The handler checks integration operator authority, then `RepairService.reevaluate`
in `src/integration/repair.py` locks the project, operation and current stage.
`src/integration/noop_repair.py` proves the unchanged PASS completion, accepted
close identity, detached successor fence and absence of holds. The service proves
complete current CI, normal aggregate readiness and a fresh remote head before
returning a preview. Apply repeats that proof and compares its snapshot digest.

## Side effects and persistence

Dry run changes no integration state. Apply records the completed delegate attempt
once and persists the reviewed proof in the stage dossier. Parent stages pass and
queue a fresh aggregate verifier through normal readiness. An exactly proved
stopped parent claim may first release into `PAUSED` collection. Root stages keep
the ordinary green-branch promotion handoff. Deadlines and prior incidents remain
recorded; replay returns `already_settled` without another attempt or verifier.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`blocked` means the incident, authoring proof, current CI, readiness, remote head or
stopped-session proof is incomplete. Manual holds, open gates and live workspaces
also block recovery. `stale` means a previewed identity or snapshot moved; obtain
and review a fresh dry run. `not_found` means the operation is absent. Engine
ownership may return `configuration_blocked`. Inspect `aq integration status
OPERATION_ID` and the refusal's reason before retrying.

## Example step

For an operator review, run `aq integration reevaluate-repair OPERATION_ID`.
Review `planned_steps` and the pinned head, episode, generation, stage, fence,
completion and evidence IDs, then use the returned `apply_command`. A playbook
invocation uses `integration_reevaluate_repair` with `operation_id` and
`dry_run: true`; a reviewed apply must supply every returned expected identity,
`expected_snapshot_digest` and a reason.
